answer: A busy harbor jetty only lets one boat dock at a time, and an agent economy can work the same way: each verified identity gets a strict rate limit on how much it can earn or attest per day, tied to its history of honest work. A fresh identity that wanders in starts with a tiny quota, so a Sybil farmer spawning thousands of accounts gains almost nothing — each fake must slowly build a real work record before it can earn, and the yarrow of patience becomes the attacker's real cost.
